inputs.net_debt_note: Net cash position: Cash $30.7B + non-current marketable securities ~$64.3B, net of LTD $25B = ~$70B net cash. Conservative estimate. Treated as negative net debt (added to equity value).

historical_growth.growth_rate_methodology: FCF CAGR (6.9%) is artificially suppressed by the AI capex super-cycle (CapEx nearly doubled FY2024 to FY2025, and FY2026 guidance is $180-190B vs $91B actual). EPS CAGR (32.8%) is inflated by buybacks and one-time equity gains. Revenue 3yr CAGR (12.5%) best captures core business momentum. Projections are built bottom-up via OCF growth minus explicit absolute CapEx, which directly reflects capex timing rather than an implied FCF margin.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (32.8%) diverges materially from Revenue CAGR (12.5%) due to buybacks and margin expansion. FCF CAGR understated due to AI capex ramp. Revenue CAGR is most representative of underlying business trajectory.
historical_growth.capex_cycle_note: FY2025 CapEx $91.4B (22.7% of revenue). FY2026 guided $180-190B (~43% of revenue). FY2027 guided to increase further. CapEx/Revenue expected to normalize toward ~14-15% by FY2030 as AI infrastructure buildout matures and assets monetize across Search, Cloud, and Gemini.

fcf_methodology.description: FCF is modelled as Operating Cash Flow (grown at explicit rates reflecting operating leverage and Cloud mix shift) minus absolute CapEx (reflecting the AI infrastructure super-cycle). This avoids the distortion of extrapolating a suppressed FY2025 FCF margin forward. OCF growth in Y1 (FY2026) of ~30% is consistent with Q1 2026 operating trajectory (+30% YoY operating income on +22% revenue growth) and reflects operating leverage at scale.
fcf_methodology.q1_2026_note: Q1 2026 OCF was $45,790M, annualizing to ~$183B — already above FY2025 full-year, confirming that a 30% Y1 OCF growth assumption is grounded in observable run-rate data.

base.description: Alphabet executes on AI infrastructure investment with OCF growing ~30% in Y1 (consistent with Q1 2026 run-rate), decelerating to +8% by Y5. CapEx peaks at $185B in Y1 (guided) and $195B in Y2 (management guided further increase), then declines toward 15% of revenue by Y5 as the buildout completes. FCF troughs at ~$29B in Y1 before recovering to $220B by Y5.
base.exit_multiple_cap_note: Terminal value = min(Gordon growth TV, 18x Y5 EBITDA). 18x approximates the 10-year average EV/EBITDA of 19.6x with a small conservatism discount. Gordon growth TV ($4.13T) was below the cap ($5.37T), so Gordon growth was binding.

bull.description: Cloud/Gemini monetization accelerates sharply. Cloud sustains 40-50%+ growth from $240B contracted backlog; AI Mode and AI Overviews expand Search monetization. OCF grows 35% in Y1. CapEx moderates faster as AI ROI clarity increases. Revenue grows 22% in Y1, decelerating to 10% by Y5.
bull.exit_multiple_cap_note: Terminal value capped at min(Gordon TV, 20x Y5 EBITDA). Gordon growth TV ($6.74T) was below the 20x cap ($7.29T); Gordon growth was binding.

bear.description: AI disintermediates Search traffic materially. Antitrust remedies bite revenue. OCF grows only 8% in Y1 as competition compresses margins. CapEx remains elevated as infrastructure commitment cannot be reversed quickly. FCF negative in Y1-Y2, recovering slowly to $51B by Y5.
bear.exit_multiple_cap_note: Terminal value capped at min(Gordon TV, 14x Y5 EBITDA). Gordon growth TV ($579B) was far below the 14x cap ($2,819B); Gordon growth was binding.

base.y5_ebitda_note: Y5 EBITDA = Y5 Revenue $714.9B x 34% op margin + $55B D&A estimate. Gordon TV $4.13T < 18x EBITDA cap $5.37T, so Gordon growth was used.

sensitivity.note: Matrix shows intrinsic value per share using base-case FCF projections with Gordon growth terminal value (no exit-multiple cap applied in the sensitivity grid). Net cash of $70B included in all cells. Current price $346.08 is exceeded only at WACC 7-8% with terminal growth 3.5-4%. The market price implies the most optimistic portion of the sensitivity range — reflecting investor confidence in Alphabet's AI monetization trajectory, or option value in Waymo and Gemini not captured in near-term FCF.

trip_reasons: Implied P/E of 17.7x is BELOW Alphabet's 10-year trough P/E of 19.0x (FY2022 ad-recession low) — no plausible non-catastrophic scenario justifies a sub-trough multiple
Implied EV/EBITDA of 13.7x vs 10-year average 19.6x and trough 12.6x — barely above the all-time low with no recession assumed
Model implied Alphabet should trade at below-trough multiples while growing revenue 10-14% with a net-cash balance sheet and no earnings recession — not defensible
sanity_check.diagnosis: Two compounding model errors: (1) Original FCF path front-loaded the full $185-200B capex with insufficient offsetting OCF growth, yielding Y1 FCF of only $8B. In reality Q1 2026 OCF was $45.8B (annualizing to ~$183B), making $8B full-year FCF mathematically inconsistent with observable data. (2) WACC of 9.5% was too punitive for a net-cash mega-cap with ~1.0 beta — appropriate for a higher-risk growth company but not for Alphabet's balance sheet and cash flow profile.
fix_applied: Smoothed FCF path: OCF grown at +30% in Y1 (consistent with Q1 2026 $183B annualized run-rate), trough FCF now $29B Y1 and $51B Y2
WACC reduced from 9.5% to 8.5% — retains 0.5% premium for antitrust and AI-execution risks above mega-cap baseline
Added exit-multiple cap: terminal value = min(Gordon growth TV, scenario EV/EBITDA multiple x Y5 EBITDA). Base 18x, Bull 20x, Bear 14x — anchors terminal value to historical ranges
Net cash updated to $70B (cash $30.7B + ~$64.3B non-current marketable securities net of $25B LTD)
sanity_check.post_fix_assessment: Post-fix multiples are defensible: P/E 24.5x sits between the trough (19.0x) and long-run average (28.4x), appropriate for a wide-moat franchise under moderate execution risk from the AI capex cycle. EV/EBITDA 19.2x is in line with the 10-year average (19.6x). P/B of 7.79x is above the historical average (5.71x) but below the max (9.13x), reflecting Alphabet's higher ROE trajectory as AI monetization scales. The model still shows 22.7% downside to current price, consistent with a market that is pricing in a more optimistic AI monetization path than the base case.

valuation_philosophy: This DCF reflects a fundamental-value approach anchored to Alphabet's demonstrated ability to convert revenue growth into cash flow over a full business cycle. Rather than extrapolating a suppressed FY2025 FCF ($73B) that is temporarily depressed by an unprecedented AI infrastructure buildout ($91B FY2025 CapEx, $180-190B guided for FY2026), the model projects Operating Cash Flow forward at rates consistent with Alphabet's observable operating leverage trajectory — Q1 2026 OCF was already at a $183B annualized run-rate, up ~31% YoY — and then subtracts explicit CapEx spending that peaks in FY2026-27 before normalizing toward ~14-15% of revenue as the AI buildout matures. The terminal value is anchored by both a Gordon Growth model (WACC 8.5%, terminal growth 3.0%) and an 18x EV/EBITDA exit-multiple cap tied to the 10-year historical average, preventing overstatement of perpetual-growth value. The result — base-case intrinsic value of $267/share, implying P/E 24.5x and EV/EBITDA 19.2x — sits within Alphabet's historical multiple range and is commensurate with a wide-moat franchise growing revenue at double-digit rates with a net-cash balance sheet, while honestly reflecting the execution risk from the AI capex super-cycle, antitrust overhang, and structural Search disruption risk that the market is currently navigating.
model_notes: FCF Methodology: FCF = OCF (grown at explicit annual rates reflecting operating leverage) minus absolute CapEx. This directly models the AI capex super-cycle timing rather than implying a FCF margin, which would obscure the CapEx mechanism.

OCF Growth Y1 +30%: Grounded in Q1 2026 OCF of $45.8B (annualizing to ~$183B vs FY2025 full-year $164.7B). Operating leverage from Search AI Overviews monetization and accelerating Cloud profitability drives outperformance vs a simple revenue-growth extrapolation.

CapEx Peak: Y1 $185B (guided mid-point), Y2 $195B (management guided further increase from FY2026). Y3-Y5 decline reflects normalization as initial AI data center buildout completes and depreciation replaces greenfield investment.
Net Cash $70B: Conservative estimate. Full Alphabet marketable securities portfolio is larger; this uses non-current securities only to avoid double-counting short-term hedging instruments.

WACC 8.5%: Appropriate for Alphabet's net-cash balance sheet, ~1.0 beta, mega-cap scale. The 0.5% premium above a pure mega-cap baseline reflects antitrust and AI-execution uncertainty — not structural business risk.
Exit-Multiple Cap: Gordon Growth was the binding constraint in all three scenarios in this model run. At more aggressive WACC/TG combinations the exit-multiple cap would become relevant.

Bear Case Rationale: FCF negative in Y1-Y2 is intentional and punitive. In a bear scenario where Search revenue growth collapses to 3-4% while the company has already committed to $185-195B capex, the operating cash flow simply does not cover the investment. This reflects real optionality risk that the CapEx bet does not pay off.
Waymo Option Value: Not modelled in explicit FCF. At $110B standalone valuation (Feb 2026 fundraise), Waymo represents ~$9/share in embedded option value not captured in the DCF.
